sentence_of_record_previous: On the union EVAL mix (6,139 items, 5,628 components), the content-closed v2 tree's flatLeaf files at 0.812 [0.801, 0.822], +9.4pp [+8.3, +10.5] over descent, while class-conditional spherical k-means that reads the TRAIN labels files better by 2.15pp [1.25, 3.01] [ARCH-V2-E-T-R2, POSTRUN_rp12_r2 78a30da1 VALID; surface-sensitive, untested on capability text; a union-mix figure (MMLU-Pro 0.745, GPQA 0.673, MATH 0.621); G10 byte-identical on the declared set for 7 pairs, never "deterministic"; G12 and FLAT pending]

plain_description.what: A full rebuild of the version-2 query tree on the clean data split (no duplicate questions shared between building and testing), after a fix to how its quality metrics are computed. It checks that the tree rebuilds identically, how well it files new questions into the right class, whether a k-means clustering that is allowed to read the class labels does better, and whether any top-level split is statistically certified.
plain_description.why: The previous build failed the 'rebuilds identically' check. The thesis needs a reproducible tree before any claim about it can stand, plus an honest comparison against simpler clustering.
plain_description.information: A tree that rebuilds identically and files well would support using it as the evaluation's address book. Losing to label-reading k-means, or having no certified splits, would mean its structure mostly comes from the declared labels it is anchored on. Result: done. The tree rebuilt byte-identically on the 7 pairs checked (never a general 'deterministic' claim). It filed 81.2% of new questions correctly, about 9.4 points better than step-by-step descent through the tree. This is a mixed-corpus figure: 74.5% on MMLU-Pro alone. Label-reading k-means filed about 2 points better. No top-level split was certified. Its leaves were somewhat purer than a flat mixture-model control (one build, one draw, thin margin), with no gain on key information. Note: the tree is anchored on declared labels, so 'label-free' only means no LLM labelling.
